title: Testing for Grit
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece treats grit as a genuinely valuable but hard-to-assess hiring trait, and walks through several ways leaders try to detect it before someone joins the team. Reference checks, behavioral interview questions about walked-away challenges, and puzzle-based case studies all get a mention as imperfect but useful tools. The author lists a set of habits -- long-range goal setting, deliberate gratitude, framing situations optimistically, and openly sharing intrinsic motivation -- as observable proxies for the harder-to-see quality of persistence. The piece closes with a wink about the irony of how much effort it takes to reliably test for effort itself.
points: Grit is a person's ability to persevere toward long-term goals despite setbacks and obstacles.
Common assessment methods include reference stories, behavioral interview questions, and case-study puzzles.
Gritty candidates tend to share observable habits like long-range goal setting and deliberate gratitude.
Because grit is hard to see directly, leaders should use several assessment methods together.
quotes: The idea of grit refers to a person’s ability to persevere and remain determined in the face of challenge, adversity, or obstacles.
Those with grit bounce back from setbacks, displaying a resilience to cope with whatever is thrown at them.
In behavioral interviews, leaders can learn when candidates have walked away from a challenge and why.
Some leaders and organizations prefer to use puzzles or case studies to test for grit.
The quality of grit, or a passionate persistence, is considered a priceless attribute when hiring prospective team members.
People with grit maintain a commitment to long-term goals and consistently work toward them despite the difficulties that may arise along the way.
They don’t allow obstacles to become a distraction or to derail them from achieving their goals.
Gritty team members share a host of positive assets, including a growth mindset and the ability to maintain a deeper focus on long-term goals.
